chapters.name: Dice
sections: Type 1 – Only One Position is Given
Type 2 – Two Positions, One Number Common
Type 3 – Two Positions, Two Numbers Common
Type 4 – Two Positions, No Number Common

qs.q: How many faces does a cube have?
qs.s: A cube (dice) has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 corners.

qs.q: How many edges does a cube have?
qs.s: 4 edges on the top face + 4 on the bottom face + 4 vertical edges = 12.

qs.q: In any one position of a dice, at the most how many of its faces can be seen?
qs.s: Only top, front and right (3 faces) are visible; the other 3 are hidden.

qs.q: How many faces of a dice are adjacent to (share an edge with) any one face?
qs.s: Every face touches 4 faces along its edges; only the opposite face does not touch it.

qs.q: In a standard dice, which number is opposite to 5?
qs.s: On a standard dice opposite faces add up to 7: 7 − 5 = 2.

qs.q: On a standard dice, which of the following pairs can NEVER be seen together?
qs.s: 1 + 6 = 7, so 1 and 6 are opposite faces; opposite faces are never seen together.

qs.q: On a standard dice, which pair cannot be on opposite faces?
qs.s: Opposite faces add up to 7; 2 + 6 = 8, so 2 and 6 cannot be opposite.

qs.q: A standard dice rests on a table with 5 on its top face. Which number touches the table?
qs.s: The bottom face is opposite the top: 7 − 5 = 2.

qs.q: Three standard dice are thrown and the top faces show 2, 5 and 1. What is the sum of the numbers on their bottom faces?
Four standard dice show 6, 2, 4 and 1 on their top faces. What is the sum of the bottom faces?
The dice shown below is a —
o: May be standard or normal dice
qs.s: 2 and 5 are visible together, so they are adjacent. On a standard dice 2 + 5 = 7 would be opposite — so this is a normal dice.

qs.q: The dice shown below is a —
o: May be standard or normal dice
qs.s: Visible pairs 1+2, 2+4, 1+4 — none adds up to 7, so no rule is broken; but the hidden faces are not shown, so it may be standard or normal.

qs.q: Which of the following can be a standard dice?
qs.s: (a) shows 1 & 6, (b) shows 4 & 3 and (c) shows 5 & 2 together — each pair adds up to 7, so they break the rule. Only (d) can be standard.

qs.q: A standard dice shows 6 on the top, 2 in the front and 4 on the right. What is the sum of the numbers on the three hidden faces?
qs.s: Hidden faces are opposite to 6, 2, 4 → 1, 5, 3. Sum = 1 + 5 + 3 = 9.

qs.q: One position of a dice is shown. Which number can NOT be opposite to 5?
qs.s: 5, 6 and 4 are seen together, so 6 is adjacent to 5 and can never be opposite to it.

qs.q: One position of a dice is shown. Which letter is opposite to C?
qs.s: Only one position is given. A and E are adjacent to C; its opposite is one of B, D, F — it cannot be fixed.

qs.q: One position of a dice is shown. Which of the following is certainly adjacent to 3?
qs.s: 3, 1 and 5 are seen together, so 1 is adjacent to 3. The hidden numbers 2, 4 and 6 may or may not be adjacent.

qs.q: One position of a dice is shown. How many different numbers can possibly be opposite to 4?
qs.s: 2 and 6 are seen with 4, so they are adjacent. The opposite of 4 can be any of the 3 hidden numbers (1, 3, 5).

qs.q: If the dice shown below is a standard dice, which number is at the bottom?
qs.s: Standard dice: bottom = 7 − top = 7 − 3 = 4.

qs.q: If the dice shown below is a standard dice, what is the sum of the numbers on the three hidden faces?
qs.s: Hidden faces are opposite to 5, 1 and 3 → 2, 6 and 4. Sum = 12.

qs.q: One position of a dice is shown. Which symbol can NOT be at the bottom when ★ is on the top?
qs.s: ★ and ▲ are seen together, so ▲ is adjacent to ★; the bottom face is opposite the top, so ▲ can never be there.

qs.q: One position of a dice is shown. Which of the following statements is definitely true?
qs.s: P, Q and R are visible together, so R is adjacent to P. The other statements need hidden faces and cannot be confirmed.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which number is opposite to 3?
qs.s: 5 is common. Clockwise from 5: (i) 5 → 6 → 2, (ii) 5 → 3 → 1. So 6 ↔ 3, 2 ↔ 1 and 5 ↔ 4 (the unseen one). Hence the opposite of 3 is 6.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which number will be on the face opposite to 3?
qs.s: 5 is common. Clockwise from 5: (i) 5 → 4 → 2, (ii) 5 → 6 → 3. So 4 ↔ 6, 2 ↔ 3 and 5 ↔ 1 (the unseen one). Hence the opposite of 3 is 2.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which number is opposite to 5?
qs.s: 4 is common. Clockwise from 4: (i) 4 → 3 → 1, (ii) 4 → 2 → 5. So 3 ↔ 2, 1 ↔ 5 and 4 ↔ 6 (the unseen one). Hence the opposite of 5 is 1.

qs.q: Two different positions of the same dice are shown below. Find the number opposite to 3.
qs.s: 6 is common. Clockwise from 6: (i) 6 → 5 → 4, (ii) 6 → 3 → 1. So 5 ↔ 3, 4 ↔ 1 and 6 ↔ 2 (the unseen one). Hence the opposite of 3 is 5.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which number will be on the face opposite to 2?
qs.s: 5 is common. Clockwise from 5: (i) 5 → 2 → 4, (ii) 5 → 1 → 3. So 2 ↔ 1, 4 ↔ 3 and 5 ↔ 6 (the unseen one). Hence the opposite of 2 is 1.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which number will be on the face opposite to 5?
qs.s: 3 is common. Clockwise from 3: (i) 3 → 5 → 2, (ii) 3 → 4 → 6. So 5 ↔ 4, 2 ↔ 6 and 3 ↔ 1 (the unseen one). Hence the opposite of 5 is 4.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which number is opposite to 4?
qs.s: 4 is common. Clockwise from 4: (i) 4 → 1 → 6, (ii) 4 → 5 → 3. So 1 ↔ 5, 6 ↔ 3 and 4 ↔ 2 (the unseen one). Hence the opposite of 4 is 2.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. If 4 is on the top, which number will be at the bottom?
qs.s: 1 is common. Clockwise from 1: (i) 1 → 2 → 5, (ii) 1 → 6 → 4. So 2 ↔ 6, 5 ↔ 4 and 1 ↔ 3 (the unseen one). Bottom is opposite to top, so it is 5.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Find the numbers opposite to 3, 5 and 2 respectively.
qs.s: 2 is common. Clockwise from 2: (i) 2 → 4 → 1, (ii) 2 → 5 → 3. So 4 ↔ 5, 1 ↔ 3 and 2 ↔ 6 (the unseen one). So the answer is 1, 4, 6.

qs.q: Two different positions of the same dice are shown below. Find the letter opposite to C.
qs.s: F is common. Clockwise from F: (i) F → C → E, (ii) F → A → B. So C ↔ A, E ↔ B and F ↔ D (the unseen one). Hence the opposite of C is A.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which letter will be on the face opposite to T?
qs.s: S is common. Clockwise from S: (i) S → U → T, (ii) S → P → Q. So U ↔ P, T ↔ Q and S ↔ R (the unseen one). Hence the opposite of T is Q.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. If M is on the top, which letter will be at the bottom?
qs.s: S is common. Clockwise from S: (i) S → R → Q, (ii) S → M → P. So R ↔ M, Q ↔ P and S ↔ N (the unseen one). Bottom is opposite to top, so it is R.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which symbol will be on the face opposite to ♥ ?
qs.s: ● is common. Clockwise from ●: (i) ● → ◆ → ▲, (ii) ● → ♥ → ★. So ◆ ↔ ♥, ▲ ↔ ★ and ● ↔ ■ (the unseen one). Hence the opposite of ♥ is ◆.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which symbol will be on the face opposite to *?
qs.s: $ is common. Clockwise from $: (i) $ → % → *, (ii) $ → & → @. So % ↔ &, * ↔ @ and $ ↔ # (the unseen one). Hence the opposite of * is @.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Find the numbers opposite to 2, 4 and 1 respectively.
qs.s: 1 is common. Clockwise from 1: (i) 1 → 6 → 3, (ii) 1 → 2 → 5. So 6 ↔ 2, 3 ↔ 5 and 1 ↔ 4 (the unseen one). So the answer is 6, 1, 4.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which letter is opposite to P?
qs.s: O is common. Clockwise from O: (i) O → P → K, (ii) O → L → M. So P ↔ L, K ↔ M and O ↔ N (the unseen one). Hence the opposite of P is L.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which of the following positions is possible?
qs.s: 2 is common. Clockwise from 2: (i) 2 → 6 → 4, (ii) 2 → 3 → 5. So 6 ↔ 3, 4 ↔ 5 and 2 ↔ 1 (the unseen one). Reject options showing an opposite pair: (a) shows 1 and 2; (b) shows 5 and 4; (d) shows 1 and 2. Only (c) is possible.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which of the following positions is possible?
qs.s: 3 is common. Clockwise from 3: (i) 3 → 4 → 2, (ii) 3 → 5 → 1. So 4 ↔ 5, 2 ↔ 1 and 3 ↔ 6 (the unseen one). Reject options showing an opposite pair: (a) shows 5 and 4; (c) shows 3 and 6; (d) shows 1 and 2. Only (b) is possible.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which of the following positions is possible?
qs.s: D is common. Clockwise from D: (i) D → A → F, (ii) D → E → B. So A ↔ E, F ↔ B and D ↔ C (the unseen one). Reject options showing an opposite pair: (a) shows B and F; (b) shows A and E; (d) shows A and E. Only (c) is possible.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which of the following positions is NOT possible?
qs.s: 5 is common. Clockwise from 5: (i) 5 → 6 → 1, (ii) 5 → 4 → 3. So 6 ↔ 4, 1 ↔ 3 and 5 ↔ 2 (the unseen one). Option (a) shows 3 and 1 together, which are opposite — so it is NOT possible.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which of the following positions is possible?
qs.s: ▲ is common. Clockwise from ▲: (i) ▲ → ♥ → ●, (ii) ▲ → ■ → ◆. So ♥ ↔ ■, ● ↔ ◆ and ▲ ↔ ★ (the unseen one). Reject options showing an opposite pair: (a) shows ★ and ▲; (c) shows ★ and ▲; (d) shows ★ and ▲. Only (b) is possible.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which of the following positions is NOT possible?
qs.s: 2 is common. Clockwise from 2: (i) 2 → 5 → 3, (ii) 2 → 1 → 6. So 5 ↔ 1, 3 ↔ 6 and 2 ↔ 4 (the unseen one). Option (b) shows 3 and 6 together, which are opposite — so it is NOT possible.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which of the following positions is possible?
qs.s: R is common. Clockwise from R: (i) R → Q → S, (ii) R → U → T. So Q ↔ U, S ↔ T and R ↔ P (the unseen one). Reject options showing an opposite pair: (a) shows R and P; (b) shows R and P; (d) shows U and Q. Only (c) is possible.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which of the following positions is NOT possible?
qs.s: 3 is common. Clockwise from 3: (i) 3 → 6 → 1, (ii) 3 → 2 → 4. So 6 ↔ 2, 1 ↔ 4 and 3 ↔ 5 (the unseen one). Option (a) shows 6 and 2 together, which are opposite — so it is NOT possible.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which number is opposite to 1?
qs.s: 2 and 5 are common to both positions, so the remaining numbers 1 and 6 are opposite.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which number is opposite to 2?
qs.s: 1 and 3 are common to both positions, so the remaining numbers 2 and 4 are opposite.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which number is opposite to 3?
qs.s: 2 and 5 are common to both positions, so the remaining numbers 4 and 3 are opposite.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which letter is opposite to B?
qs.s: C and E are common to both positions, so the remaining letters B and F are opposite.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which number is opposite to 4?
qs.s: 1 and 5 are common to both positions, so the remaining numbers 4 and 6 are opposite.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which symbol is opposite to $?
qs.s: & and * are common to both positions, so the remaining symbols $ and # are opposite.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which letter is opposite to Q?
qs.s: N and S are common to both positions, so the remaining letters M and Q are opposite.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which number is opposite to 2?
qs.s: 5 and 6 are common to both positions, so the remaining numbers 2 and 1 are opposite.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which letter is opposite to E?
qs.s: C and E are common, so F ↔ A. The opposite of E is one of the unseen letters B or D; both possibilities are given together as "B or D".

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which number is opposite to 6?
qs.s: 1 and 6 are common, so 2 ↔ 3. The opposite of 6 is one of the unseen numbers 4 or 5; no "4 or 5" option is given, so the answer is "Cannot be determined".

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which number is opposite to 2?
qs.s: 2 and 4 are common, so 6 ↔ 1. The opposite of 2 is one of the unseen numbers 3 or 5; neither "3 or 5" nor "Cannot be determined" is given, so the answer is "None of these".

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which letter is opposite to K?
qs.s: K and L are common, so M ↔ N. The opposite of K is one of the unseen letters O or P; no "O or P" option is given, so the answer is "Cannot be determined".

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which number is opposite to 5?
qs.s: 5 and 6 are common, so 2 ↔ 4. The opposite of 5 is one of the unseen numbers 1 or 3; neither "1 or 3" nor "Cannot be determined" is given, so the answer is "None of these".

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which number is opposite to 5?
qs.s: 2 and 5 are common, so 4 ↔ 1. The opposite of 5 is one of the unseen numbers 3 or 6; only 6 is a possible number among the options, so choose 6.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which letter is opposite to M?
qs.s: M and S are common, so P ↔ Q. The opposite of M is one of the unseen letters N or R; both possibilities are given together as "N or R".

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which number is opposite to 3?
qs.s: 3 and 5 are common, so 2 ↔ 4. The opposite of 3 is one of the unseen numbers 1 or 6; only 1 is a possible number among the options, so choose 1.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which number is opposite to 4?
qs.s: No number is common, so the six numbers are split 3 + 3. The opposite of 4 is one of 6, 5, 3 — it cannot be fixed.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which number can NOT be opposite to 3?
qs.s: 5 is seen with 3 in position (i), so they are adjacent and can never be opposite. Each of 6, 4, 1 may be opposite.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. Which letter is opposite to D?
qs.s: No letter is common, so the six letters are split 3 + 3. The opposite of D is one of E, C, A — it cannot be fixed.

qs.q: Two positions of a dice are shown. The opposite of 3 must be one of which group?
qs.s: No number is common. 3 is adjacent to 4 and 2, so its opposite must be one of 1, 5, 6.

qs.q: Three different positions of dice are shown below. Which number appears on the face opposite to the number 6?
qs.s: Positions (i) and (ii) both show 3 and 5, so the remaining numbers 1 and 6 are opposite.

qs.q: Three positions of the same dice are shown. Which number is opposite to 2?
qs.s: Use positions (i) and (ii): 1 is common; clockwise from 1: 1 → 6 → 4 and 1 → 2 → 5 → 2 ↔ 6. Hence the opposite of 2 is 6.

qs.q: Three positions of the same dice are shown. Which number is opposite to 4?
qs.s: Positions (i) and (ii) have 2 and 3 common, so the remaining 4 and 5 are opposite. Hence the opposite of 4 is 5.

qs.q: Three positions of the same dice are shown. Which number is opposite to 5?
qs.s: Use positions (i) and (ii): 4 is common; clockwise from 4: 4 → 1 → 2 and 4 → 5 → 6 → 5 ↔ 1. Hence the opposite of 5 is 1.

qs.q: Three positions of the same dice are shown. Which number is opposite to 2?
qs.s: Use positions (i) and (iii): 2 is common; clockwise from 2: 2 → 4 → 3 and 2 → 6 → 1 → 2 ↔ 5. Hence the opposite of 2 is 5.

qs.q: Three positions of the same dice are shown. Which number is opposite to 2?
qs.s: Use positions (i) and (iii): 6 is common; clockwise from 6: 6 → 4 → 3 and 6 → 5 → 1 → 2 ↔ 6. Hence the opposite of 2 is 6.

qs.q: Three positions of the same dice are shown. Which number is opposite to 2?
qs.s: Use positions (ii) and (iii): 5 is common; clockwise from 5: 5 → 4 → 1 and 5 → 6 → 3 → 2 ↔ 5. Hence the opposite of 2 is 5.

qs.q: Three positions of the same dice are shown. Which letter is opposite to U?
qs.s: Use positions (i) and (ii): Q is common; clockwise from Q: Q → P → R and Q → T → U → U ↔ R. Hence the opposite of U is R.

qs.q: Four positions of the same dice are shown. Which number is opposite to 6?
qs.s: Use positions (ii) and (iii): 4 is common; clockwise from 4: 4 → 1 → 2 and 4 → 3 → 6 → 6 ↔ 2. Hence the opposite of 6 is 2.

qs.q: Three positions of the same dice are shown. Which symbol is opposite to ■ ?
qs.s: Use positions (i) and (iii): ★ is common; clockwise from ★: ★ → ■ → ▲ and ★ → ● → ◆ → ■ ↔ ●. Hence the opposite of ■ is ●.

qs.q: Three positions of the same dice are shown. Which number is opposite to 6?
qs.s: Use positions (i) and (ii): 1 is common; clockwise from 1: 1 → 2 → 5 and 1 → 6 → 4 → 6 ↔ 2. Hence the opposite of 6 is 2.

qs.q: Four positions of the same dice are shown. Which letter is opposite to D?
qs.s: Use positions (i) and (iv): E is common; clockwise from E: E → F → C and E → A → B → D ↔ E. Hence the opposite of D is E.

qs.q: Select the cube that can be formed by folding the given sheet.
qs.s: Column S, F, B, ∧: alternate squares are opposite → S ↔ B and F ↔ ∧; row &, ∧, @ → & ↔ @. (a), (c) show S & B and (d) shows & & @ together — rejected. Only (b) is possible.

qs.q: If the following net is folded into a cube, which of the given cubes would it look like?
qs.s: One dot and three dots are in the same column with one square between → opposite. Two small squares and the filled square are alternate in the row → opposite; the two blank faces are opposite. (a), (b), (c) show an opposite pair; only (d) is possible.

qs.q: The open dice shown below is folded to form a cube. Find the number opposite to 3.
qs.s: 3 and 4 are alternate squares in the same row (one square between them). So the opposite of 3 is 4.

qs.q: The open dice shown below is folded to form a cube. Find the number opposite to 4.
qs.s: 1 and 4 are alternate squares in the same row (one square between them). So the opposite of 4 is 1.

qs.q: The given sheet is folded to form a dice. Which letter will be opposite to E?
qs.s: D and e are alternate squares in the same row (one square between them). So the opposite of E is D.

qs.q: Which cube can be formed by folding the given sheet?
qs.s: Opposite pairs: 4 ↔ 1, 6 ↔ 3, 5 ↔ 2. (a), (c), (d) show an opposite pair together, so only (b) can be formed.

qs.q: The given sheet is folded to form a dice. Which number will be opposite to 3?
qs.s: 3 and 4 are alternate squares in the same column (one square between them). So the opposite of 3 is 4.

qs.q: The given sheet is folded to form a cube. Which of the following pairs will be on opposite faces?
qs.s: 1 and 5 are alternate squares in the same column (one square between them). The other pairs touch each other in the net, so they are adjacent.

qs.q: The given sheet is folded to form a dice. Which symbol will be opposite to @?
qs.s: # and @ are alternate squares in the same row (one square between them). So the opposite of @ is #.

qs.q: Which cube can be formed by folding the given sheet?
qs.s: Opposite pairs: Q ↔ S, P ↔ T, U ↔ R. (a), (b), (c) show an opposite pair together, so only (d) can be formed.

qs.q: The given sheet is folded to form a dice. Which number will be opposite to 5?
qs.s: 2 and 5 are alternate squares in the same row (one square between them). So the opposite of 5 is 2.

qs.q: The given sheet is folded to form a cube. Which of the following pairs will be on opposite faces?
qs.s: M and s are alternate squares in the same column (one square between them). The other pairs touch each other in the net, so they are adjacent.

qs.q: The given sheet is folded to form a dice. Which number will be opposite to 5?
qs.s: Z-shape 1–3–6–5: the first and the last squares are opposite. So the opposite of 5 is 1.

qs.q: The given sheet is folded to form a dice. Which number will be opposite to 1?
qs.s: Z-shape 1–5–3–6: the first and the last squares are opposite. So the opposite of 1 is 6.

qs.q: The open dice shown below is folded to form a cube. Find the letter opposite to D.
qs.s: Z-shape a–f–e–d: the first and the last squares are opposite. So the opposite of D is A.

qs.q: The given sheet is folded to form a cube. Which of the following pairs will be on opposite faces?
qs.s: Z-shape 1–5–6–3: the first and the last squares are opposite. The other pairs touch each other in the net, so they are adjacent.

qs.q: The open dice shown below is folded to form a cube. Find the number opposite to 6.
qs.s: Z-shape 4–3–1–6: the first and the last squares are opposite. So the opposite of 6 is 4.

qs.q: Which cube can be formed by folding the given sheet?
qs.s: Opposite pairs: 3 ↔ 6, 2 ↔ 1, 5 ↔ 4. (a), (b), (c) show an opposite pair together, so only (d) can be formed.

qs.q: If the sheet shown below is folded to form a cube, which symbol will be on the face opposite to ◆ ?
qs.s: Z-shape ▲–■–♥–◆: the first and the last squares are opposite. So the opposite of ◆ is ▲.

qs.q: If the sheet shown below is folded to form a cube, which number will be on the face opposite to 1?
qs.s: Z-shape 1–4–6–2: the first and the last squares are opposite. So the opposite of 1 is 2.

qs.q: Which cube can be formed by folding the given sheet?
qs.s: Opposite pairs: M ↔ K, L ↔ O, P ↔ N. (a), (b), (d) show an opposite pair together, so only (c) can be formed.

qs.q: The given sheet is folded to form a cube. Which of the following pairs will be on opposite faces?
qs.s: Z-shape 1–6–2–3: the first and the last squares are opposite. The other pairs touch each other in the net, so they are adjacent.

chapters.name: Calendar
sections: Day of the Week on a Given Date

qs.q: How many days are there in a normal (non-leap) year?
qs.s: A normal year has 365 days (February has 28 days).

qs.q: A normal year has —
qs.s: 365 = 52 × 7 + 1, so 52 weeks and 1 extra day.

qs.q: How many months of a year have 31 days?
qs.s: January, March, May, July, August, October and December — 7 months.

qs.q: How many months of a year have exactly 30 days?
qs.s: April, June, September and November have 30 days.

qs.q: Which of the following is a leap year?
qs.s: 2020 ÷ 4 = 505 with no remainder, so 2020 is a leap year; the others leave a remainder.

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT a leap year?
qs.s: 2026 ÷ 4 leaves remainder 2, so it is a normal year.

qs.q: How many days are there in a leap year?
qs.s: A leap year has 366 days because February has 29 days.

qs.q: How many days does February have in a leap year?
qs.s: The extra day of a leap year is 29 February.

qs.q: Which statement correctly describes the year 2024?
o: It is a leap year with 366 days
It is a normal year with 365 days
qs.s: 2024 is not a century year and is divisible by 4 → leap year (366 days).

qs.q: A leap year has —
qs.s: 366 = 52 × 7 + 2, so 52 weeks and 2 extra days.

qs.q: In which of the following years does February have 29 days?
qs.s: 2028 ÷ 4 = 507 with no remainder → leap year → February has 29 days.

qs.q: A year that is not a century year and is divisible by 4 is called a —
qs.s: A non-century year divisible by 4 is a leap year.

qs.q: How many leap years can there be in 7 consecutive years (no century year in between)?
qs.s: 7 ÷ 4 → quotient 1, remainder 3. A remainder is left, so it can be 1 or 2.

qs.q: How many leap years are there from 2001 to 2024 (both years included)?
How many leap years are there in 16 consecutive years (no century year in between)?
qs.s: 16 ÷ 4 = 4 with no remainder, so there are exactly 4 leap years.

qs.q: What is the maximum number of leap years in 10 consecutive years (no century year in between)?
qs.s: 10 ÷ 4 → quotient 2, remainder 2 → 2 or 3; the maximum is 3 (e.g. 2004–2013: 2004, 2008, 2012).

qs.q: How many leap years are there from 1990 to 2010 (both years included)?
qs.s: Leap years: 1992, 1996, 2000, 2004, 2008 → 5 (2000 is divisible by 400, so it is a leap year).

qs.q: What is the minimum number of leap years in 9 consecutive years (no century year in between)?
qs.s: 9 ÷ 4 → quotient 2, remainder 1 → 2 or 3; the minimum is 2.

qs.q: Which of the following century years is a leap year?
qs.s: A century year is a leap year only if divisible by 400: 2000 ÷ 400 = 5.

qs.q: Which statement correctly describes the year 1900?
o: It is a leap year with 366 days
It is a normal year with 365 days
qs.s: 1900 is a century year not divisible by 400, so it is a normal year (365 days).

qs.q: How many leap years are there from 1801 to 1900 (both years included)?
qs.s: 25 years are divisible by 4, but 1900 is not a leap year → 24.

qs.q: How many leap years are there from 1901 to 2000 (both years included)?
qs.s: 25 years are divisible by 4 and 2000 is a leap year (divisible by 400) → 25.

qs.q: The last day of a century can NOT be —
qs.s: 100, 200, 300, 400 years have 5, 3, 1, 0 odd days → the last day is Friday, Wednesday, Monday or Sunday — never Tuesday, Thursday or Saturday.

qs.q: How many odd days are there in 45 days?
qs.s: 45 = 6 weeks + 3 days → 3 odd days.

qs.q: How many odd days are there in 100 days?
qs.s: 100 = 14 weeks + 2 days → 2 odd days.

qs.q: How many odd days are there in a leap year?
qs.s: 366 = 52 weeks + 2 days → 2 odd days.

qs.q: How many odd days are there in the month of April?
qs.s: April has 30 days = 4 weeks + 2 days → 2.

qs.q: How many odd days are there from 1 January to 30 June of a normal year (both days included)?
How many odd days are there in a normal year?
qs.s: 365 = 52 weeks + 1 day → 1 odd day.

qs.q: How many odd days are there in February of a leap year?

qs.q: In a certain code language, 'la ma ra' means 'blue girl flows', 'ra da sa' means 'blue is big' and 'sa la ka' means 'is girl ball'. What is the code for 'flows'?
qs.s: 'blue girl flows' and 'blue is big' have the common word 'blue' and the common code 'ra'. Comparing the sentences step by step, 'flows' = ma.

qs.q: In a certain code language, 'ta na la' means 'is fast cap', 'na ma ra' means 'is mango red' and 'ka ta ra' means 'mango fast small'. What is the code for 'fast'?
qs.s: 'is fast cap' and 'is mango red' have the common word 'is' and the common code 'na'. Comparing the sentences step by step, 'fast' = ta.

qs.q: In a certain code language, 'da sa na' means 'cap tall apple', 'ta da ra' means 'cap runs flows' and 'ka la ta' means 'flows red good'. What is the code for 'red'?
qs.s: The word 'red' appears in only one sentence together with another word that also appears only there, so its code cannot be fixed.

qs.s: Interchanging × and ÷: 3 + 19 × 4 ÷ 2 − 19 = 22 ✓ (the other choices do not give 22).

Which direction is exactly opposite to North-East?
qs.s: Opposite of North is South and of East is West → South-West.

qs.q: If you are facing North, your right hand will be towards —
qs.s: Facing North, the right side is East and the left side is West.

qs.q: What is the angle between North and South-East, measured clockwise?
qs.s: N → E is 90°, E → SE is 45° more → 135°.

qs.q: Which direction lies exactly between South and West?
qs.s: The sub-direction between South and West is South-West.

qs.q: If a person is facing South, which direction is to his left?
qs.s: Facing South, the left hand points East (and the right hand West).

qs.q: In the morning the Sun rises in the —
qs.s: The Sun rises in the East and sets in the West.

qs.q: Ravi wants to go to the university. He starts from his home which is in the East and comes to a crossing. The road to the left ends in a theatre, straight ahead is the hospital. In which direction is the university?
qs.s: Coming from the East he walks West; left = South (theatre), straight = West (hospital), back = East (home) → the remaining road, North, leads to the university.

qs.q: A person is facing South-East. He turns to his left. Which direction is he facing now?
qs.s: Start South-East; left turn (−90°) → North-East.

qs.q: A person is facing North. He turns to his right and then again to his right. Which direction is he facing now?
qs.s: Start North; right turn (+90°), right turn (+90°) → South.

qs.q: A person is facing South. He turns to his left. Which direction is he facing now?
qs.s: Start South; left turn (−90°) → East.

qs.q: A person is facing North-West. He turns to his left and then again to his left. Which direction is he facing now?
qs.s: Start North-West; left turn (−90°), left turn (−90°) → South-East.

qs.q: A person is facing East. He turns to his left. Which direction is he facing now?
qs.s: Start East; left turn (−90°) → North.

qs.q: A person is facing South. He turns to his right, then to his left. Which direction is he facing now?
qs.s: Start South; right turn (+90°), left turn (−90°) → South.

qs.q: A person is facing East. He turns to his left. Which direction is he facing now?
qs.s: Start East; left turn (−90°) → North.

qs.q: A person is facing South. He turns to his right. Which direction is he facing now?
qs.s: Start South; right turn (+90°) → West.

qs.q: A person is facing West. He turns to his right. Which direction is he facing now?
qs.s: Start West; right turn (+90°) → North.

qs.q: A person is facing North. He walks 50 m, turns to his right and walks 25 m and finally turns to his left and walks 15 m. In which direction is he moving now?
qs.s: Turns: 1 right, 1 left → net no turn → North.

qs.q: A person is facing South. He walks 50 m, turns to his right and walks 40 m, turns to his right and walks 40 m, turns to his left and walks 15 m and finally turns to his left and walks 25 m. In which direction is he moving now?
qs.s: Turns: 2 right, 2 left → net no turn → South.

qs.q: A person is facing West. He walks 50 m, turns to his left and walks 15 m, turns to his left and walks 10 m and finally turns to his left and walks 40 m. In which direction is he moving now?
qs.s: Turns: 0 right, 3 left → net 1 right → North.

qs.q: A person is facing East. He walks 20 m, turns to his left and walks 20 m and finally turns to his right and walks 15 m. In which direction is he moving now?
qs.s: Turns: 1 right, 1 left → net no turn → East.

qs.q: A person is facing East. He walks 50 m, turns to his left and walks 40 m, turns to his right and walks 10 m and finally turns to his right and walks 30 m. In which direction is he moving now?
qs.s: Turns: 2 right, 1 left → net 1 right → South.

qs.q: A person is facing South. He walks 20 m, turns to his right and walks 15 m, turns to his right and walks 40 m and finally turns to his right and walks 40 m. In which direction is he moving now?
qs.s: Turns: 3 right, 0 left → net 1 left → East.

qs.q: A person is facing South. He walks 50 m, turns to his right and walks 15 m, turns to his left and walks 50 m, turns to his left and walks 30 m and finally turns to his left and walks 25 m. In which direction is he moving now?
qs.s: Turns: 1 right, 3 left → net 2 turns (opposite) → North.

qs.q: A person is facing East. He walks 20 m, turns to his right and walks 10 m, turns to his right and walks 20 m and finally turns to his left and walks 40 m. In which direction is he moving now?
qs.s: Turns: 2 right, 1 left → net 1 right → South.

qs.q: A person is facing South. He walks 30 m, turns to his left and walks 20 m and finally turns to his right and walks 20 m. In which direction is he moving now?
qs.s: Turns: 1 right, 1 left → net no turn → South.

qs.q: A person is facing West. He walks 10 m, turns to his left and walks 20 m, turns to his left and walks 30 m and finally turns to his left and walks 15 m. In which direction is he moving now?
qs.s: Turns: 0 right, 3 left → net 1 right → North.

qs.q: A person is facing South-West. He walks 50 m, turns to his right and walks 30 m, turns to his right and walks 30 m, turns to his left and walks 20 m and finally turns to his left and walks 10 m. In which direction is he moving now?
qs.s: Turns: 2 right, 2 left → net no turn → South-West.

qs.q: A person is facing South-West. He walks 10 m, turns to his left and walks 20 m, turns to his right and walks 20 m, turns to his left and walks 50 m and finally turns to his right and walks 30 m. In which direction is he moving now?
qs.s: Turns: 2 right, 2 left → net no turn → South-West.

qs.q: A person is facing North-East. He walks 20 m, turns to his right and walks 50 m, turns to his right and walks 30 m, turns to his left and walks 50 m and finally turns to his left and walks 20 m. In which direction is he moving now?
qs.s: Turns: 2 right, 2 left → net no turn → North-East.

qs.q: A person is facing North-West. He walks 40 m, turns to his left and walks 50 m and finally turns to his right and walks 40 m. In which direction is he moving now?
qs.s: Turns: 1 right, 1 left → net no turn → North-West.

qs.q: A person takes the turns left, right, left, left and is finally facing South. In which direction was he facing at the start?
qs.s: Net turn = 1 right − 3 left → reverse it from South → North. Check: North + turns = South ✓.

qs.q: A person takes the turns right, right, left and is finally facing East. In which direction was he facing at the start?
qs.s: Net turn = 2 right − 1 left → reverse it from East → North. Check: North + turns = East ✓.

qs.q: A person takes the turns right, left, right and is finally facing North. In which direction was he facing at the start?
qs.s: Net turn = 2 right − 1 left → reverse it from North → West. Check: West + turns = North ✓.

qs.q: A person takes the turns right, right, left, right, left and is finally facing South. In which direction was he facing at the start?
qs.s: Net turn = 3 right − 2 left → reverse it from South → East. Check: East + turns = South ✓.

qs.q: A person takes the turns left, left and is finally facing North. In which direction was he facing at the start?
qs.s: Net turn = 0 right − 2 left → reverse it from North → South. Check: South + turns = North ✓.

qs.q: A person takes the turns right, left, right, right and is finally facing West. In which direction was he facing at the start?
qs.s: Net turn = 3 right − 1 left → reverse it from West → East. Check: East + turns = West ✓.

qs.q: A person takes the turns right, right, left and is finally facing North. In which direction was he facing at the start?
qs.s: Net turn = 2 right − 1 left → reverse it from North → West. Check: West + turns = North ✓.

qs.q: A person takes the turns left, left and is finally facing South-East. In which direction was he facing at the start?
qs.s: Net turn = 0 right − 2 left → reverse it from South-East → North-West. Check: North-West + turns = South-East ✓.

qs.q: A person takes the turns left, right, right, right and is finally facing North-West. In which direction was he facing at the start?
qs.s: Net turn = 3 right − 1 left → reverse it from North-West → South-East. Check: South-East + turns = North-West ✓.

qs.q: A person takes the turns left, left, right and is finally facing North-West. In which direction was he facing at the start?
qs.s: Net turn = 1 right − 2 left → reverse it from North-West → North-East. Check: North-East + turns = North-West ✓.

qs.q: A person is facing South-East. He turns 90° anticlockwise, then 90° clockwise, then 90° anticlockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
qs.s: Clockwise 90°, anticlockwise 180° → net 90° anticlockwise → North-East.

qs.q: A person is facing South-West. He turns 180° clockwise, then 45° anticlockwise, then 90° clockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
qs.s: Clockwise 270°, anticlockwise 45° → net 225° clockwise → East.

qs.q: A person is facing East. He turns 45° anticlockwise, then 45° clockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
qs.s: Clockwise 45°, anticlockwise 45° → net 0° clockwise → East.

qs.q: A person is facing South. He turns 135° anticlockwise, then 90° clockwise, then 180° anticlockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
qs.s: Clockwise 90°, anticlockwise 315° → net 225° anticlockwise → North-West.

qs.q: A person is facing South-East. He turns 135° anticlockwise, then 135° clockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
qs.s: Clockwise 135°, anticlockwise 135° → net 0° clockwise → South-East.

qs.q: A person is facing North-East. He turns 180° clockwise, then 90° clockwise, then 45° anticlockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
qs.s: Clockwise 270°, anticlockwise 45° → net 225° clockwise → West.

qs.q: A person is facing South-East. He turns 180° clockwise, then 135° anticlockwise, then 90° clockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
qs.s: Clockwise 270°, anticlockwise 135° → net 135° clockwise → West.

qs.q: A person is facing North. He turns 180° anticlockwise, then 90° clockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
qs.s: Clockwise 90°, anticlockwise 180° → net 90° anticlockwise → West.

qs.q: A person is facing East. He turns 135° clockwise, then 180° clockwise, then 90° anticlockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
qs.s: Clockwise 315°, anticlockwise 90° → net 225° clockwise → North-West.

qs.q: A person is facing West. He turns 45° clockwise, then 90° clockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
qs.s: Clockwise 135°, anticlockwise 0° → net 135° clockwise → North-East.

qs.q: A man walked 60 m to the East from point A, then turned right and walked 50 m. At last he turned left and went 60 m and reached point B. Find AB.
qs.s: B is 120 m East and 50 m South of A → AB = √(120² + 50²) = 130 m.

qs.q: A man steadily goes 8 m due east and 6 m due north. What is the distance between initial and final point?
If Q is exactly to the east of M and M is exactly to the south of R, then towards which direction is Q from R?
qs.s: R is north of M and Q is east of M → Q is South-East of R.

qs.q: Going 50 m to the South of my house, I turn left and go another 20 m. Then turning to the North, I go 30 m and then start walking to my house. In which direction am I walking now?
qs.s: I end 20 m East and 20 m South of the house, so I walk towards North-West.

qs.q: Of the five villages P, Q, R, S and T situated close to each other, P is to the west of Q, R is to the south of P, T is to the north of Q and S is to the east of T. Then, R is in which direction with respect to S?
qs.s: Taking Q at the centre: P west, R south of P, T north of Q, S east of T → R is South-West of S.

qs.q: The town of Paranda is located on Green Lake. The town of Akram is west of Paranda. Tokhada is east of Akram but west of Paranda. Kakran is east of Bopri but west of Tokhada and Akram. If they are all in the same district, which town is the farthest west?
qs.s: West → East: Bopri, Kakran, Akram, Tokhada, Paranda → Bopri is farthest west.

qs.q: A person is facing West. He walks 16 m and finally turns to his right and walks 30 m. How far is he from the starting point?
qs.s: He ends 16 m West and 30 m North of the start → distance = √(16² + 30²) = 34 m, towards North-West.

qs.q: A person is facing West. He walks 100 m and finally turns to his right and walks 105 m. How far and in which direction is he from the starting point?
qs.s: He ends 100 m West and 105 m North of the start → distance = √(100² + 105²) = 145 m, towards North-West.

qs.q: A person is facing East. He walks 105 m, turns to his left and walks 40 m and finally turns to his left and walks 75 m. How far is he from the starting point?
qs.s: He ends 30 m East and 40 m North of the start → distance = √(30² + 40²) = 50 m, towards North-East.

qs.q: A person is facing North. He walks 100 m and finally turns to his right and walks 105 m. How far and in which direction is he from the starting point?
qs.s: He ends 105 m East and 100 m North of the start → distance = √(105² + 100²) = 145 m, towards North-East.

qs.q: A person is facing North. He walks 8 m and finally turns to his right and walks 15 m. How far is he from the starting point?
qs.s: He ends 15 m East and 8 m North of the start → distance = √(15² + 8²) = 17 m, towards North-East.

qs.q: A person is facing South. He walks 200 m, turns to his left and walks 120 m and finally turns to his left and walks 150 m. How far and in which direction is he from the starting point?
qs.s: He ends 120 m East and 50 m South of the start → distance = √(120² + 50²) = 130 m, towards South-East.

qs.q: A person is facing South. He walks 30 m and finally turns to his left and walks 40 m. How far is he from the starting point?
qs.s: He ends 40 m East and 30 m South of the start → distance = √(40² + 30²) = 50 m, towards South-East.

qs.q: A person is facing North. He walks 9 m and finally turns to his left and walks 12 m. How far and in which direction is he from the starting point?
qs.s: He ends 12 m West and 9 m North of the start → distance = √(12² + 9²) = 15 m, towards North-West.

qs.q: A person is facing North. He walks 10 m, turns to his right and walks 12 m and finally turns to his right and walks 5 m. How far is he from the starting point?
qs.s: He ends 12 m East and 5 m North of the start → distance = √(12² + 5²) = 13 m, towards North-East.

qs.q: A person is facing South. He walks 150 m and finally turns to his right and walks 200 m. How far and in which direction is he from the starting point?
qs.s: He ends 200 m West and 150 m South of the start → distance = √(200² + 150²) = 250 m, towards South-West.

qs.q: A person is facing South. He walks 40 m and finally turns to his left and walks 42 m. How far is he from the starting point?
qs.s: He ends 42 m East and 40 m South of the start → distance = √(42² + 40²) = 58 m, towards South-East.

qs.q: A person is facing North. He walks 80 m, turns to his left and walks 40 m and finally turns to his left and walks 50 m. How far and in which direction is he from the starting point?
qs.s: He ends 40 m West and 30 m North of the start → distance = √(40² + 30²) = 50 m, towards North-West.

qs.q: A person is facing North. He walks 60 m and finally turns to his left and walks 80 m. How far is he from the starting point?
qs.s: He ends 80 m West and 60 m North of the start → distance = √(80² + 60²) = 100 m, towards North-West.

qs.q: A person is facing South. He walks 6 m and finally turns to his right and walks 8 m. How far and in which direction is he from the starting point?
qs.s: He ends 8 m West and 6 m South of the start → distance = √(8² + 6²) = 10 m, towards South-West.

qs.q: C is 20 km West of B. P is 21 km North of C. How far and in which direction is P from B?
qs.s: P is 20 km West and 21 km North of B → √(20² + 21²) = 29 km, North-West.

qs.q: P is 3 km West of C. S is 4 km North of P. How far and in which direction is S from C?
qs.s: S is 3 km West and 4 km North of C → √(3² + 4²) = 5 km, North-West.

qs.q: S is 15 km North of D. R is 20 km East of S. How far and in which direction is R from D?
qs.s: R is 20 km East and 15 km North of D → √(20² + 15²) = 25 km, North-East.

qs.q: B is 6 km West of R. C is 8 km South of B. How far and in which direction is C from R?
qs.s: C is 6 km West and 8 km South of R → √(6² + 8²) = 10 km, South-West.

qs.q: In the evening at 4 PM, Reema's shadow falls directly behind her. Which direction is she facing?
qs.s: In the evening the Sun is in the West; the shadow behind her means she faces the Sun → West.

qs.q: In the evening at 4 PM, Seeta and Reema are sitting in a garden facing each other. If Reema's shadow falls behind her, which direction is Seeta facing?
qs.s: Reema faces West (towards the evening Sun); Seeta faces Reema, i.e. East.

qs.q: If West becomes East, South becomes North and so on, then what will North-West become?
qs.s: Every direction turns 180° clockwise (West → East). So North-West → South-East.

qs.q: If West becomes North, South-West becomes North-West and so on, then what will South-East become?
qs.s: Every direction turns 90° clockwise (West → North). So South-East → South-West.

qs.q: If North-West becomes East, South-East becomes West and so on, then what will West become?
qs.s: Every direction turns 135° clockwise (North-West → East). So West → North-East.

qs.q: If South-West becomes West, South-East becomes South and so on, then what will North-East become?
qs.s: Every direction turns 45° clockwise (South-West → West). So North-East → East.

qs.q: If South-West becomes North-West, South becomes West and so on, then what will South-East become?
qs.s: Every direction turns 90° clockwise (South-West → North-West). So South-East → South-West.

qs.q: If North becomes East, East becomes South and so on, then what will South-West become?
qs.s: Every direction turns 90° clockwise (North → East). So South-West → North-West.

qs.q: If South-East becomes North-East, North-West becomes South-West and so on, then what will North-East become?
qs.s: Every direction turns 90° anticlockwise (South-East → North-East). So North-East → North-West.

qs.q: One morning, a man was standing in a field and his shadow fell to his right. Which direction was he facing?
qs.s: In the morning the Sun is in the East, so shadows fall towards the West. The shadow is to his right → he is facing South.

qs.q: One evening, a man was standing in a field and his shadow fell to his right. Which direction was he facing?
qs.s: In the evening the Sun is in the West, so shadows fall towards the East. The shadow is to his right → he is facing North.

qs.q: One evening, a man was standing in a field and his shadow fell behind him. Which direction was he facing?
qs.s: In the evening the Sun is in the West, so shadows fall towards the East. The shadow is behind him → he is facing West.

qs.q: One evening, a man was standing in a field and his shadow fell to his left. Which direction was he facing?
qs.s: In the evening the Sun is in the West, so shadows fall towards the East. The shadow is to his left → he is facing South.

qs.q: One morning a man is walking towards North. On which side of him does his shadow fall?
qs.s: In the morning shadows fall towards the West. Walking North, the West is to his left.

qs.q: One evening a man is walking towards East. On which side of him does his shadow fall?
qs.s: In the evening shadows fall towards the East. Walking East, the East is in front of him.

qs.q: One morning a man is walking towards West. On which side of him does his shadow fall?
qs.s: In the morning shadows fall towards the West. Walking West, the West is in front of him.

qs.q: How many vowels are there in the English alphabet?
qs.s: A, E, I, O, U → 5 vowels.

qs.q: What is the position of the letter T in the English alphabet?
qs.s: EJOTY: T = 20.

qs.q: Which letter is 8th from the right end of the English alphabet?
qs.s: From the right: 27 − 8 = 19th from the left = S.

qs.q: Which letter is exactly in the middle of the English alphabet (13th from the left)?
qs.s: 13th letter = M (and N is 13th from the right).

qs.q: What is the position of Q from the right end of the English alphabet?
qs.s: Q is 17th from the left → 27 − 17 = 10th from the right.

qs.q: How many letters are there between D and K in the English alphabet?
qs.s: E, F, G, H, I, J → 6 letters (11 − 4 − 1).

How many consonants are there in the English alphabet?
qs.s: 26 − 5 vowels = 21 consonants.

qs.q: Which of the following letters is a vowel?
qs.s: U is a vowel; K, W, Y are consonants.

qs.q: If the English alphabet is written in reverse order (Z to A), which letter will be 5th from the left?
qs.s: Reverse order: Z, Y, X, W, V → 5th is V.

qs.q: Which letter will be 12th to the left of the 12th letter from the right end of the English alphabet?
qs.s: 12th from the right = 15 from the left (27 − 12); 12th to the left → 15 − 12 = 3 → C.

qs.q: Which letter will be 12th to the right of the 20th letter from the right end of the English alphabet?
qs.s: 20th from the right = 7 from the left (27 − 20); 12th to the right → 7 + 12 = 19 → S.

qs.q: Which letter will be 8th to the left of the 4th letter from the right end of the English alphabet?
qs.s: 4th from the right = 23 from the left (27 − 4); 8th to the left → 23 − 8 = 15 → O.

qs.q: Which letter will be 6th to the right of the 17th letter from the left end of the English alphabet?
qs.s: 17th from the left = 17; 6th to the right → 17 + 6 = 23 → W.

qs.q: Which letter will be 9th to the right of the 15th letter from the left end of the English alphabet?
qs.s: 15th from the left = 15; 9th to the right → 15 + 9 = 24 → X.

qs.q: Which letter will be 3rd to the left of the 12th letter from the left end of the English alphabet?
qs.s: 12th from the left = 12; 3rd to the left → 12 − 3 = 9 → I.

qs.q: Which letter will be 3rd to the right of the 15th letter from the right end of the English alphabet?
qs.s: 15th from the right = 12 from the left (27 − 15); 3rd to the right → 12 + 3 = 15 → O.

qs.q: Which letter will be 7th to the right of the 15th letter from the left end of the English alphabet?
qs.s: 15th from the left = 15; 7th to the right → 15 + 7 = 22 → V.

qs.q: Which letter will be 12th to the left of the 14th letter from the left end of the English alphabet?
qs.s: 14th from the left = 14; 12th to the left → 14 − 12 = 2 → B.

qs.q: Which letter will be 4th to the right of the 20th letter from the left end of the English alphabet?
qs.s: 20th from the left = 20; 4th to the right → 20 + 4 = 24 → X.

qs.q: Which letter will be 12th to the right of the 11th letter from the left end of the English alphabet?
qs.s: 11th from the left = 11; 12th to the right → 11 + 12 = 23 → W.

qs.q: Which letter will be 6th to the right of the 15th letter from the right end of the English alphabet?
qs.s: 15th from the right = 12 from the left (27 − 15); 6th to the right → 12 + 6 = 18 → R.

qs.q: Which letter will be 4th to the left of the 15th letter from the right end of the English alphabet?
qs.s: 15th from the right = 12 from the left (27 − 15); 4th to the left → 12 − 4 = 8 → H.

qs.q: Which letter will be 5th to the right of the 16th letter from the left end of the English alphabet?
qs.s: 16th from the left = 16; 5th to the right → 16 + 5 = 21 → U.

qs.q: Which letter will be 11th to the left of the 19th letter from the left end of the English alphabet?
qs.s: 19th from the left = 19; 11th to the left → 19 − 11 = 8 → H.

qs.q: Which letter will be 3rd to the left of the 7th letter from the right end of the English alphabet?
qs.s: 7th from the right = 20 from the left (27 − 7); 3rd to the left → 20 − 3 = 17 → Q.

qs.q: If the English alphabet is written in reverse order, which letter will be 4th to the left of the 14th letter from the left end?
qs.s: Reversed alphabet Z, Y, X … ; position 14 − 4 = 10 → Q.

qs.q: If the digits in the number 42168674 are arranged in descending order from left to right, what will be the product of the digits which are 3rd from the left end and 4th from the right end in the new arrangement?
qs.s: Descending: 8 7 6 6 4 4 2 1 → 3rd from left = 6, 4th from right = 4 → 6 × 4 = 24.

qs.q: If the digits of the number 42824531 are arranged in ascending order from left to right, what will be the difference of the digits which are 2nd from the left end and 4th from the right end?

qs.q: In syllogism, which of the following statements is a universal statement?
qs.s: All and No give complete (100%) information → universal.

qs.q: In the statement "All A are B", the subject A is —
qs.s: All A are B → A = 100, B = 50.

qs.q: In the statement "Some A are not B", the object B is —
qs.s: Negative statement → its object is always 100.

qs.q: Which word in a syllogism statement means the same as "Some"?
qs.s: Some = at least one, many, a few, most …

qs.q: In a syllogism question, the given statements should be —
o: taken as true even if they look odd
qs.s: We always accept the statements as true.

qs.q: Which pair of conclusions can form an "either–or" case?
o: All A are B / Some A are B
No A are B / No B are A
Some A are B / Some B are A
Some A are B / No A are B
qs.s: Either–or needs a complementary pair on the same terms: Some + No, or All + Some-not.

qs.q: A conclusion follows only when it is —
qs.s: A possibility is not enough; it must be definitely true.

qs.q: "All cats are animals." Which statement is the correct conversion?
qs.s: All → Some: cats 100, animals 50 → Some animals are cats.

qs.q: Statement: Some birds are not fruits. Conclusion I: Some fruits are birds. Conclusion II: All birds are fruits. Which conclusion(s) follow?
o: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
qs.s: I: Some fruits are birds → only a possibility, not definite ✗. II: All birds are fruits → definitely false ✗.

qs.q: Statement: No hills are pens. Conclusion I: All pens are hills. Conclusion II: Some hills are not pens. Which conclusion(s) follow?
o: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
qs.s: I: All pens are hills → definitely false ✗. II: Some hills are not pens → definitely true ✓.

qs.q: Statement: No kites are plates. Conclusion I: All plates are kites. Conclusion II: Some plates are not kites. Which conclusion(s) follow?
o: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
qs.s: I: All plates are kites → definitely false ✗. II: Some plates are not kites → definitely true ✓.

qs.q: Statement: No plates are walls. Conclusion I: No walls are plates. Conclusion II: Some plates are not walls. Which conclusion(s) follow?
o: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
qs.s: I: No walls are plates → definitely true ✓. II: Some plates are not walls → definitely true ✓.

qs.q: Statement: Some flowers are doors. Conclusion I: Some flowers are not doors. Conclusion II: Some doors are flowers. Which conclusion(s) follow?
o: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows

Both Statements I and II are necessary
qs.s: Even together: a × a × b = 125 can be 5 × 5 × 5 (cube) or 1 × 1 × 125 (not a cube).

qs.q: How much time did X take to reach a certain destination? Statement I: The ratio between the speeds of X and Y is 3 : 5. Statement II: Y takes 45 minutes to reach the destination.
o: Statement I alone is sufficient while Statement II alone is not sufficient

Statement II alone is sufficient, while Statement I alone is not sufficient
Either of the Statements I or II alone is sufficient
qs.s: Time ∝ 1/speed: X takes 45 × 5/3 = 75 minutes — needs both statements.

qs.q: Three towns P, Q and R are on a straight line. Town R is between P and Q. The distance from P to R is 100 km. How far is Q from P? Statement I: The distance between R and Q is 50% more than the distance between P and R. Statement II: Five times the distance from P to R is the same as two times the distance between P and Q.
o: Statement I alone is sufficient while Statement II alone is not sufficient
Both Statements I and II are necessary
Either Statement I or II alone is sufficient to answer
Statement II alone is sufficient while Statement I alone is not sufficient
qs.s: I: RQ = 150 → PQ = 250. II: 5 × 100 = 2 × PQ → PQ = 250. Each alone works.

Both Statements I and II are not sufficient
qs.s: The principal is not given, so the rate cannot be found even with both statements.

qs.s: The speeds of the trains are not known, so the length of A cannot be found.

qs.q: What is the rate of interest percent per annum? Statement I: Difference between the compound interest and the simple interest earned on a certain amount in 2 years is ₹ 500. Statement II: An amount doubles itself in 5 years on simple interest. Statement III: Simple interest earned per annum is ₹ 2000.
o: Statement II only, or Statements I and III only are sufficient
All three statements I, II and III are necessary
Any two of the three statements are necessary
qs.s: II alone: an amount doubles in 5 years on SI → R = 100 ÷ 5 = 20%. I and III together: CI − SI = P(R/100)² and SI per year = PR/100, so R can be found from them. Hence II alone, or I and III together.

qs.q: Pointing to a photograph of a boy, Suresh said, "He is the son of the only son of my mother." How is Suresh related to that boy?
qs.s: The only son of Suresh's mother is Suresh himself → the boy is Suresh's son → Suresh is the father.

qs.q: Gopal said, pointing to Govind, "His father is my father's only son." How is Gopal related to Govind?
qs.s: My father's only son = Gopal himself → Govind's father is Gopal.

qs.q: Pointing to a man, Rina said, "He is the son of my grandfather's only son." How is the man related to Rina?
qs.s: Grandfather's only son = Rina's father → his son is Rina's brother.

qs.q: Introducing a girl, Tamo said, "Her father is the only son of my father." How is the girl related to Tamo?
qs.s: Only son of Tamo's father = Tamo himself → the girl is his daughter.

qs.q: Pointing to a photograph, a man said, "Her mother is the only daughter of my mother." How is the girl in the photograph related to the man?
qs.s: Only daughter of his mother = his sister → the girl is his sister's daughter → niece.

qs.q: Pointing to a woman, Arun said, "She is the daughter of the only child of my grandmother." How is the woman related to Arun?
qs.s: Only child of Arun's grandmother = Arun's parent → her daughter is Arun's sister.

qs.q: Pointing to a boy, Meena said, "He is the son of the only son of my father." How is the boy related to Meena?
qs.s: Only son of Meena's father = Meena's brother → his son is her nephew.

qs.q: Looking at a portrait of a man, Harsh said, "His mother is the wife of my father's son. I have no brothers or sisters." How is the man related to Harsh?
qs.s: My father's son = Harsh (no siblings) → his mother is Harsh's wife → the man is Harsh's son.

qs.q: Introducing a man, a woman said, "His wife is the only daughter of my father." How is the man related to the woman?
qs.s: The only daughter of her father is the woman herself → the man is her husband.

qs.q: Pointing to a man in a photograph, Asha said, "His brother's father is the only son of my grandfather." How is the man related to Asha?
qs.s: Only son of Asha's grandfather = Asha's father → he is the man's father too → brother.

qs.q: Pointing to an old man, Kiran said, "His son is my son's uncle." How is the old man related to Kiran?
qs.s: My son's uncle is my brother (taking Kiran as the father); the old man's son is my brother → the old man is my father.

qs.q: If A + B means A is mother of B, A ÷ B means A is brother of B, A × B means A is the son of B and A − B means A is daughter of B, which of the following means C is the niece of D?
qs.s: C − P: C is the daughter of P; P ÷ D: P is the brother of D → C is D's niece.

qs.q: If A @ B means A is brother of B, and A $ B means A is wife of B, then what does X @ Y $ Z mean?
o: X is brother of Y and Y is wife of Z
qs.s: Read two at a time: X @ Y and Y $ Z.

qs.q: "A @ B" means A is the mother of B, "A # B" means A is the father of B, "A % B" means A is the son of B. How is X related to Z in X % Y % Z?
o: X is the grandson of Z
X is the son of Z
X is the father of Z
X is not related to Z
qs.s: X is the son of Y and Y is the son of Z → X is Z's grandson.

qs.q: If A × D means 'A is the sister of D', A + D means 'D is the daughter of A' and A ÷ D means 'A is the mother of D', then how will 'N is the aunt of M' be denoted?
qs.s: N × L: N is the sister of L; L ÷ M: L is the mother of M → N is M's aunt.

qs.q: If 'A − B' means 'A is the father of B', 'A # B' means 'A is the brother of B', 'A × B' means 'A is the husband of B', 'A + B' means 'A is the daughter of B', then in the expression P + T # V, how is P related to V?
qs.s: P + T: P is the daughter of T; T # V: T is the brother of V → P is the niece of V.

qs.q: If 'A $ B' means 'A is the father of B', 'A ÷ B' means 'A is the wife of B', 'A + B' means 'A is the son of B', 'A × B' means 'A is the mother of B', then in the expression T ÷ V $ R, how is T related to R?
qs.s: T ÷ V: T is the wife of V; V $ R: V is the father of R → T is the mother of R.

qs.q: If 'A + B' means 'A is the husband of B', 'A − B' means 'A is the brother of B', 'A × B' means 'A is the mother of B', 'A @ B' means 'A is the wife of B', then in the expression V × P − S, how is V related to S?
qs.s: V × P: V is the mother of P; P − S: P is the brother of S → V is the mother of S.

qs.q: If 'A $ B' means 'A is the husband of B', 'A × B' means 'A is the father of B', 'A @ B' means 'A is the mother of B', 'A # B' means 'A is the brother of B', then in the expression T @ U × S, how is T related to S?
qs.s: T @ U: T is the mother of U; U × S: U is the father of S → T is the grandmother of S.

qs.q: If 'A % B' means 'A is the daughter of B', 'A @ B' means 'A is the sister of B', 'A + B' means 'A is the brother of B', 'A ÷ B' means 'A is the husband of B', then in the expression T % U ÷ Q, how is T related to Q?

qs.q: If 'A × B' means 'A is the son of B', 'A @ B' means 'A is the wife of B', 'A ÷ B' means 'A is the father of B', 'A + B' means 'A is the daughter of B', then in the expression R × U × Q, how is R related to Q?

qs.q: If 'A × B' means 'A is the mother of B', 'A # B' means 'A is the sister of B', 'A − B' means 'A is the father of B', 'A % B' means 'A is the daughter of B', then in the expression S × T # U, how is S related to U?

qs.q: If 'A + B' means 'A is the daughter of B', 'A @ B' means 'A is the brother of B', 'A × B' means 'A is the husband of B', 'A # B' means 'A is the mother of B', then in the expression R # Q @ U, how is R related to U?

qs.q: If 'A @ B' means 'A is the sister of B', 'A ÷ B' means 'A is the daughter of B', 'A $ B' means 'A is the brother of B', 'A # B' means 'A is the son of B', then in the expression R @ V ÷ T, how is R related to T?

qs.s: Codes are row first, then column. (b) fails at 23 (23 is P); (c) fails at 96 (96 is N); (d) fails at 32 (32 is P). Only (a) gives SING.

qs.q: In a row of students in a class, Ravi is 17th from either end of the row. How many students are there in the class?
In a row, Kamal is 37th from both the ends. How many persons are there in the row?
In a queue, Deepak is 26th from the front and 31st from the back. How many persons are there in the queue?
In a class, Anu is 26th from the top and 7th from the bottom. How many students are there in the class?
In a row, Amit is 37th from both the ends. How many persons are there in the row?

In a row, Nabam is 28th from both the ends. How many persons are there in the row?

There are 21 persons in a row. Riya is 9th from the top. What is her rank from the bottom?
qs.s: Rank from the bottom = (21 + 1) − 9 = 13.

qs.q: There are 26 persons in a row. Anu is 3rd from the top. What is his rank from the bottom?
qs.s: Rank from the bottom = (26 + 1) − 3 = 24.

qs.q: There are 46 persons in a row. Rina is 10th from the bottom. What is her rank from the top?
qs.s: Rank from the top = (46 + 1) − 10 = 37.

qs.q: There are 49 persons in a row. Riya is 18th from the bottom. What is his rank from the top?
qs.s: Rank from the top = (49 + 1) − 18 = 32.

qs.q: There are 33 persons in a row. Tage is 7th from the left. What is her rank from the right?
qs.s: Rank from the right = (33 + 1) − 7 = 27.

qs.q: There are 48 persons in a row. Anu is 45th from the bottom. What is his rank from the top?
qs.s: Rank from the top = (48 + 1) − 45 = 4.

qs.q: There are 40 persons in a row. Tadar is 34th from the left. What is her rank from the right?
qs.s: Rank from the right = (40 + 1) − 34 = 7.

qs.q: There are 46 persons in a row. Ravi is 24th from the left. What is his rank from the right?
qs.s: Rank from the right = (46 + 1) − 24 = 23.

qs.q: There are 53 persons in a row. Tadar is 49th from the right. What is her rank from the left?
qs.s: Rank from the left = (53 + 1) − 49 = 5.

qs.q: There are 31 persons in a row. Anu is 17th from the bottom. What is his rank from the top?
qs.s: Rank from the top = (31 + 1) − 17 = 15.

qs.q: There are 49 persons in a row. Tadar is 16th from the bottom. What is her rank from the top?
qs.s: Rank from the top = (49 + 1) − 16 = 34.

qs.q: There are 30 persons in a row. Pooja is 24th from the bottom. What is his rank from the top?
qs.s: Rank from the top = (30 + 1) − 24 = 7.

qs.q: There are 52 persons in a row. Tenzin is 18th from the top. What is her rank from the bottom?
qs.s: Rank from the bottom = (52 + 1) − 18 = 35.

qs.q: There are 22 persons in a row. Anu is 12th from the left. What is his rank from the right?
qs.s: Rank from the right = (22 + 1) − 12 = 11.

qs.q: In a row, Rina is 6th from the left and Amit is 7th from the right. They interchange their positions and now Rina is 16th from the left. How many persons are there in the row?
qs.s: After the interchange Rina is at Amit's old place: 16th from the left and 7th from the right → total = 16 + 7 − 1 = 22.

qs.q: In a row, Tadar is 10th from the left and Nabam is 10th from the right. They interchange their positions and now Tadar is 30th from the left. How many persons are there in the row?
qs.s: After the interchange Tadar is at Nabam's old place: 30th from the left and 10th from the right → total = 30 + 10 − 1 = 39.

qs.q: In a row, Kamal is 15th from the left and Rina is 14th from the right. They interchange their positions and now Kamal is 30th from the left. How many persons are there in the row?
qs.s: After the interchange Kamal is at Rina's old place: 30th from the left and 14th from the right → total = 30 + 14 − 1 = 43.

qs.q: In a row, Kamal is 6th from the left and Anu is 15th from the right. They interchange their positions and now Kamal is 12th from the left. How many persons are there in the row?
qs.s: After the interchange Kamal is at Anu's old place: 12th from the left and 15th from the right → total = 12 + 15 − 1 = 26.

qs.q: In a row, Tadar is 14th from the left and Amit is 11th from the right. They interchange their positions and now Tadar is 26th from the left. How many persons are there in the row?
qs.s: After the interchange Tadar is at Amit's old place: 26th from the left and 11th from the right → total = 26 + 11 − 1 = 36.

qs.q: In a row, Amit is 13th from the left and Tage is 8th from the right. They interchange their positions and now Amit is 19th from the left. How many persons are there in the row?
qs.s: After the interchange Amit is at Tage's old place: 19th from the left and 8th from the right → total = 19 + 8 − 1 = 26.

qs.q: In a class of 28 students, 20 students passed. Anu passed and is 11th from the top among those who passed. What is his rank from the bottom among the students who passed?
qs.s: Only the passed students count: (20 + 1) − 11 = 10.

qs.q: In a class of 49 students, 45 students passed. Gyamar passed and is 12th from the top among those who passed. What is her rank from the bottom among the students who passed?
qs.s: Only the passed students count: (45 + 1) − 12 = 34.

qs.q: In a class of 57 students, 51 students passed. Deepak passed and is 20th from the top among those who passed. What is his rank from the bottom among the students who passed?
qs.s: Only the passed students count: (51 + 1) − 20 = 32.

qs.q: In a class of 54 students, 48 students passed. Tage passed and is 14th from the top among those who passed. What is her rank from the bottom among the students who passed?
qs.s: Only the passed students count: (48 + 1) − 14 = 35.

qs.q: Boys and girls are sitting in a row in an audience in front of a stage which faces north. Liza is fifth to the left of Reema. Reema is sitting eighth to the right of Maxwell. How many children are there between Liza and Maxwell?
qs.s: Take Maxwell at place 0: Reema at 8, Liza at 8 − 5 = 3 → children at 1 and 2 → two.

qs.q: In a row, Kamal is 5th from the left end and Mohan is 16th from the left end. How many persons are there between them?
qs.s: Persons between = 16 − 5 − 1 = 10.

qs.q: In a row, Tenzin is 10th from the left end and Nabam is 13th from the left end. How many persons are there between them?
qs.s: Persons between = 13 − 10 − 1 = 2.

qs.q: In a row, Kamal is 5th from the left end and Tadar is 14th from the left end. How many persons are there between them?
qs.s: Persons between = 14 − 5 − 1 = 8.

qs.q: In a row, Pooja is 25th from the left end and Deepak is 27th from the left end. How many persons are there between them?
qs.s: Persons between = 27 − 25 − 1 = 1.

qs.q: In a row, Deepak is 23rd from the left end and Ravi is 8th from the left end. How many persons are there between them?
qs.s: Persons between = 23 − 8 − 1 = 14.

qs.q: In a row, Gyamar is 12th from the left end and Ravi is 24th from the left end. How many persons are there between them?
qs.s: Persons between = 24 − 12 − 1 = 11.

qs.q: In a row, Rina is 27th from the left end and Pooja is 13th from the left end. How many persons are there between them?
qs.s: Persons between = 27 − 13 − 1 = 13.

qs.q: In a row, Mohan is 10th from the left end and Amit is 10th from the right end. Amit is to the right of Mohan and there are 8 persons between them. How many persons are there in the row?
In a row, Deepak is 10th from the left end and Yami is 13th from the right end. Yami is to the right of Deepak and there are 7 persons between them. How many persons are there in the row?
In a row, Kamal is 5th from the left end and Ravi is 4th from the right end. Ravi is to the right of Kamal and there are 4 persons between them. How many persons are there in the row?
In a row, Sonam is 8th from the left end and Mohan is 7th from the right end. Mohan is to the right of Sonam and there are 5 persons between them. How many persons are there in the row?
In a row, Tage is 11th from the left end and Riya is 12th from the right end. Riya is to the right of Tage and there are 8 persons between them. How many persons are there in the row?
In a row, Amit is 6th from the left end and Anu is 8th from the right end. Anu is to the right of Amit and there are 8 persons between them. How many persons are there in the row?
In a row, Tadar is 15th from the left end and Tenzin is 6th from the right end. Tenzin is to the right of Tadar and there are 3 persons between them. How many persons are there in the row?
In a row, Rina is 13th from the left end and Ravi is 13th from the right end. Ravi is to the right of Rina and there are 9 persons between them. How many persons are there in the row?
In a row of 39 persons, Ravi is 11th from the left end. Rina is 4th to the right of Ravi. What is Rina position from the right end?
qs.s: Rina is 11 + 4 = 15th from the left → from the right: (39 + 1) − 15 = 25.

qs.q: In a row of 38 persons, Sonam is 11th from the left end. Pooja is 7th to the right of Sonam. What is Pooja position from the right end?
qs.s: Pooja is 11 + 7 = 18th from the left → from the right: (38 + 1) − 18 = 21.

qs.q: In a row of 50 persons, Rina is 14th from the left end. Gyamar is 8th to the right of Rina. What is Gyamar position from the right end?
qs.s: Gyamar is 14 + 8 = 22nd from the left → from the right: (50 + 1) − 22 = 29.

qs.q: In a row of 42 persons, Rina is 14th from the left end. Sonam is 6th to the right of Rina. What is Sonam position from the right end?
qs.s: Sonam is 14 + 6 = 20th from the left → from the right: (42 + 1) − 20 = 23.

qs.q: In a row of 43 persons, Ravi is 13th from the left end. Amit is 5th to the right of Ravi. What is Amit position from the right end?
qs.s: Amit is 13 + 5 = 18th from the left → from the right: (43 + 1) − 18 = 26.

qs.q: In a row of 43 persons, Tenzin is 6th from the left end. Tadar is 4th to the right of Tenzin. What is Tadar position from the right end?
qs.s: Tadar is 6 + 4 = 10th from the left → from the right: (43 + 1) − 10 = 34.

qs.q: In a row of 30 persons, Sonam is 12th from the left end. Nabam is 3rd to the right of Sonam. What is Nabam position from the right end?
qs.s: Nabam is 12 + 3 = 15th from the left → from the right: (30 + 1) − 15 = 16.

qs.q: In a row of 49 persons, Mohan is 12th from the left end. Tenzin is 6th to the right of Mohan. What is Tenzin position from the right end?
qs.s: Tenzin is 12 + 6 = 18th from the left → from the right: (49 + 1) − 18 = 32.

qs.q: In a queue, Deepak is 21st from the front and Amit is 17th from the front. How many persons are standing between them?
qs.s: Persons between = 21 − 17 − 1 = 3.

qs.q: Roshan is taller than Hardik who is shorter than Sushil. Niza is taller than Harry but shorter than Hardik. Sushil is shorter than Roshan. Who is the tallest?
qs.s: Roshan > Sushil > Hardik > Niza > Harry → Roshan.

qs.q: P, Q, R, S and T are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. R is to the immediate left of T. P is between S and T. Who is to the immediate left of R?
qs.s: Facing the centre, left = clockwise. Clockwise order: S, P, T, R, Q → Q is to the left of R.

qs.q: A project team of 3 must be chosen from P, Q, R, S and T. If R is chosen as the first member, which is an acceptable team? (cid:127) If P is chosen, S must also be chosen. (cid:127) R and T cannot be on the same team. (cid:127) Q cannot be on the team if S is chosen.
qs.s: (b) and (d) have R with T; (c) has P without S → only R, P, S.

qs.q: In a school, five teachers A, B, C, D and E: A and B teach Hindi and English; C and B teach English and Geography; D and A teach Mathematics and Hindi; E and B teach History and French. Who teaches the maximum number of subjects?
qs.s: B teaches Hindi, English, Geography, History and French — 5 subjects.

qs.q: The high school needs to appoint a new headmaster which will be based on seniority. Mr. Karan has less seniority than Mr. Tilak but more than Mr. Bhavish. Mr. Raghav has more seniority than Mr. Karan but less than Mr. Tilak. Mr. Tilak doesn't want the job. Who will be the new headmaster?
qs.s: Tilak > Raghav > Karan > Bhavish; Tilak refuses → Raghav.

qs.q: Among Nitin, Amit, Rekha, Sudesh and Sujata, if Nitin came after Amit but not after Sujata and Rekha came after Sujata but not after Sudesh, then who came last for the performance?
qs.s: Order: Amit, Nitin, Sujata, Rekha, Sudesh → Sudesh came last.

qs.q: A is richer than B, C is richer than A, D is richer than C and E is richest of all. If they are made to sit in the above degree of richness, who will be in the middle?
qs.s: E > D > C > A > B → C is in the middle.

qs.q: Anil has invited his three friends over to watch the cricket match. A pizza shop's phone number flashes on the screen and each of the four men remembers a different number. All agree that the first three numbers are 995. Three of them agree that the fourth number is 9. Three agree that the fifth number is 2. Three agree that the sixth number is 6; three others agree that the seventh number is also 6. Which number is most likely the telephone number?
qs.s: Take the digit most of them agree on in each place: 995-9266.

qs.q: In a cricket season, India defeated Australia twice, West Indies defeated India twice, Australia defeated West Indies twice, India defeated New Zealand twice and West Indies defeated New Zealand twice. Which country has lost more number of times?
qs.s: Losses: India 2, Australia 2, West Indies 2, New Zealand 4.

qs.q: A, B, C, D, E and F, not necessarily in that order, are sitting on six chairs regularly placed around a round table. A is between D and F, C is opposite to D, and D and E are not on neighbouring chairs. Which one of the following pairs must be sitting on neighbouring chairs?
qs.s: Order around the table: D, A, F, C, E, B → C and E are neighbours.

qs.q: Seven men A, B, C, D, E, F and G are standing in a queue in that order. Each one is wearing a cap of a different colour — violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange and red. D is able to see in front of him green and blue, but not violet. E can see violet and yellow, but not red. G can see caps of all colours other than orange. If E is wearing an indigo coloured cap, then the colour of the cap worn by F is
qs.s: D = violet, G = orange, E = indigo; red is not among A–D → F wears red.

qs.q: Six roads lead to a country: X, Y, Z, 1, 2 and 3. When there is a storm, Y is blocked. When there are floods, X, 1 and 2 are affected. When road 1 is blocked, Z is also blocked. At a time when there are floods and a storm also blows, which road(s) can be used?
qs.s: Blocked: Y (storm), X, 1, 2 (floods) and Z (because 1 is blocked) → only road 3.

qs.q: George attends Music classes on Monday, Mathematics on Wednesday, History on the day following his Mathematics class and Sports on Tuesday. His Literature classes are not on Friday. If he attends just one subject in a day and his Sunday is free, then he is also free on
qs.s: Mon Music, Tue Sports, Wed Maths, Thu History, Sat Literature → Friday is free.

qs.q: In a question of a test paper, there are five items each under List-A and List-B, to be matched. No examinee has given the correct answer and answers of no two examinees are identical. What is the maximum number of examinees who took this test?
qs.s: Total ways = 5! = 120; leaving out the one correct matching → 119.

qs.q: If lights 3 and 4 are illuminated, the signal of which of the following waiters might be displayed?
qs.s: Signals containing lights 3 and 4: Amit, Dicky and Eddy.

qs.s: Light 4 on and light 1 off: Dicky (2, 3, 4) or Eddy (3, 4).

qs.s: Only one arrangement fits all the clues: E, B, C, A, D (clockwise). Answer: C.

qs.q: How many letters of the English alphabet (capitals) appear the same when looked at in a mirror?
qs.s: A, H, I, M, O, T, U, V, W, X, Y → 11 letters are left–right symmetric.

qs.q: In a mirror image (mirror on the right), which of the following changes?
qs.s: A vertical mirror swaps left and right only.

qs.q: In a water image, which of the following changes?
qs.s: Water (horizontal mirror) swaps top and bottom.

qs.q: Which of the following words will look the same (with letters only reversed in order) letter by letter in a mirror?
qs.s: Only T, O, M, A are mirror-symmetric; APPLE (P, L, E), MANGO (N, G) and KIWI (K) have letters that change.

qs.q: How many letters of the word MOTHER look exactly the same in a mirror?
qs.s: M, O, T, H are mirror-symmetric → 4.

qs.q: How many letters of the word CHOICE look exactly the same in a water image?
qs.s: C, H, O, I, C, E are all top–bottom symmetric → 6.

qs.q: Which of these letters looks the same both in a mirror and in water?
qs.s: H (also I, O, X) is symmetric both ways.

qs.q: Which digit looks the same in a water image?
qs.s: 8 is top–bottom symmetric (so are 0, 1 and 3).

qs.q: Which of the alternatives is exactly the mirror image of the given figure, when the mirror is held on the line AB?
